A dated record of what the research expected, why it expected it, and what would prove it wrong.

3 open forecasts0 resolvedFirst review · 7 November 2026

This page is a website edition of the local journal as of 31 October 2026. Updates are editorial, not automatic. Future reviews will retain the original target and probability, explain new evidence, and record mistakes and lessons.

20261031-001 · Open

October unemployment remains at or below 4.4%

65%Original probability

Registered 31 October 2026 · First review 2026-11-07

Reasoning
September unemployment is 4.2%; claims are 194,000 for October 24. Combined with Q3 private domestic demand, this argues against an abrupt near-term deterioration.
Counterevidence
September payroll growth is only 29,000 in the retrieved vintage; real household consumption barely rose. Claims can lag hiring weakness and unemployment also depends on participation.
What would falsify it?
An initial October rate above 4.4% falsifies this proposition. Assess participation, employment levels and revisions before inferring the cause.
Why this probability?
Low claims and strong quarterly domestic demand favor stability; weak hiring and softer monthly consumption limit conviction. The 4.4% threshold permits a 0.2-point increase from September. Subjective, not calibrated.
What this tests
Macro diagnostic for the growth premise; no index direction or trade follows mechanically.
Observation rule
First BLS Employment Situation release for October 2026; later revisions excluded
If data are missing
If delayed, remain open until the first release is available

Outcome: pending. No result, mistake or performance claim has been assigned.

20261031-002 · Open

Ten-year real yield remains at or above 2.50% on November 6

60%Original probability

Registered 31 October 2026 · First review 2026-11-10

Reasoning
Persistent inflation and a Fed hold with two hike dissents support a sustained real discount rate; this would keep pressure on distant equity cash flows.
Counterevidence
Weaker labor, geopolitical flight to safety or easing inflation expectations could change real yields; real yields are not controlled solely by the current policy rate.
What would falsify it?
The exact November 6 DFII10 observation below 2.50% falsifies this level forecast. Explain the cause separately; falling yields need not be bullish if growth collapses.
Why this probability?
The October 29 level is 2.63%, 13bp above the threshold. Inflation and hawkish dissents favor persistence, but modest distance to the threshold and flight-to-safety risk limit confidence. Subjective, not calibrated.
What this tests
Discount-rate diagnostic; no Treasury trade or immediate price target.
Observation rule
First published FRED DFII10 observation for the exact date; archive capture and exclude later revisions
If data are missing
Allow publication lag; no nearest-date substitute. If the first vintage cannot be established, retain unresolved and explain.

Outcome: pending. No result, mistake or performance claim has been assigned.

20261031-003 · Open

Nasdaq Composite underperforms S&P 500 from November 2 to November 20

55%Original probability

Registered 31 October 2026 · First review 2026-11-07 · Outcome review 2026-11-24

Reasoning
Elevated real yields increase the hurdle for distant cash flows. AI investment requires cash conversion, while Friday market reporting shows relative technology weakness. Hypothesis: that pressure persists beyond this week.
Counterevidence
Strong Microsoft cloud growth, lower yields or a rebound after the selloff could reverse relative performance. Nasdaq/S&P mixes size and sector exposures and does not isolate AI or cash-flow quality.
What would falsify it?
At the November 20 close, Nasdaq price return greater than or equal to S&P return from November 2 falsifies the forecast. A changed interim view remains a separate review; never change the endpoints.
Why this probability?
Real-yield and capex-funding risks suggest mild continued relative pressure, but the recent selloff may already reflect them and demand remains strong. Only a small subjective tilt above 50%; no pricing edge demonstrated.
What this tests
Research-only relative price-index comparison. No dividends, fees, financing, beta hedge or executable portfolio P&L. Monday close is a prospective measurement baseline, not a claimed entry fill.
Observation rule
Exact-date FRED NASDAQCOM and SP500 daily closing observations, first captured after publication; archive both endpoints and report revisions separately
If data are missing
Capture November 2 closes after publication; wait for exact November 20 closes. Never silently substitute a nearby date or Nasdaq-100.

Outcome: pending. No result, mistake or performance claim has been assigned.

How the record will be reviewed

Outcome accuracy and reasoning quality are separate. A correct call may rest on weak reasoning; a probabilistic miss is not automatically a flawed process. Each review will assess the evidence, timing, chosen expression and what should change.

Once an exact outcome is available, the binary Brier score is (original probability − outcome)², with outcome equal to 1 for a hit and 0 for a miss. Lower scores are better. A constant 50% forecast scores 0.25. Three related forecasts are insufficient to establish calibration or a persistent investment edge.

Missing observations remain unresolved. Data revisions and corrections will be dated; a new view cannot silently replace an original forecast. No simulated or live trading returns are claimed.
